contract.known_boundary: Audio capture/playback and device-routing boundary with explicit format negotiation.

candidates.raspberry_pi_evidence: official PortAudio Raspberry Pi wiki plus pinned ALSA/input/output source evidence

research_findings.capture_playback: The two Flutter families cover capture/playback on the six standard Flutter targets. miniaudio and PortAudio independently provide native capture/playback evidence for Raspberry Pi adaptation.
research_findings.device_routing: flutter-webrtc has explicit device enumeration and input/output selection. miniaudio exposes separate playback/capture device enumeration. PortAudio exposes host-independent device indices and input/output stream parameters. Exact platform.audio_io.v1 routing semantics remain draft.
research_findings.format_negotiation: audio_io provides explicit PCM/sample-rate evidence; miniaudio and PortAudio expose native format conversion/configuration capabilities. Exact Library contract conformance is not asserted while the contract remains draft.
research_findings.raspberry_pi: Target discovery depth is now 2/2 using two independent native families: miniaudio explicitly lists Raspberry Pi on the exact pinned release commit, and PortAudio maintains an official Raspberry Pi guide using ALSA. Neither result is treated as proof that a Flutter adapter already exists or works.
research_findings.security: The Flutter candidates remain vulnerability REVIEW due unresolved Pub versions. The two Raspberry Pi native candidates remain source/security REVIEW: miniaudio has a test Gradle wrapper binary plus a zero-byte blob reader limitation, while PortAudio contains process execution in test tooling; native supply-chain analysis is not yet supported. No candidate is security admitted or certified.

decision.next_action: Keep platform.audio_io discovery depth closed but admission open: correct the zero-byte blob reader false positive, add native C/CMake supply-chain evidence, separately review opaque/test execution findings, then design and hardware-test the Raspberry Pi adapter behind the draft platform.audio_io.v1 boundary before any Library intake.
